Powered by the Qualcomm Snapdragon 695 5G chipset (Octa-core), it runs on Android 13 upgradable to version 14 and supports dual-SIM connectivity via Nano-SIM or eSIM in a model that is IP68 dust/water resistant with dimensions of 155 x 68 x 8.3 mm. Connectivity is robust with GSM/HSPA/LTE/5G support across multiple bands including SA/NSA configurations, Wi-Fi dual-band, Bluetooth 5.1 aptX Adaptive, GPS/GLONASS/GALILEO/BDS/QZSS positioning, NFC, and USB Type-C OTG capabilities. text: The Motorola Razr 40 Ultra is a foldable smartphone featuring a main display with a 6.9-inch LTPO AMOLED panel offering 1080 x 2640 pixels resolution at 165Hz, paired with an external secondary screen measuring 3.6 inches and running at 144Hz. Powered by the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8+ Gen 1 chipset on Android 13, it supports up to 12GB of RAM across storage configurations ranging from 256GB to 512GB using UFS 3.1 technology. The device houses a dual-camera system with a 12MP wide sensor and a 13MP ultrawide lens for photography, while the front-facing camera is a single 32MP unit capable of recording 4K video at up to 60fps. With dimensions that unfold to 170.8 x 74 mm (folded size is 88.4 x 74 mm) and weighing approximately 185 grams, the phone includes a non-removable 3800 mAh battery supporting both 30W wired charging and 5W wireless charging. Connectivity options include GSM/CDMA/HSPA/LTE/5G networks with extensive band support for international and North American regions, Wi-Fi 6e, Bluetooth 5.3, GPS/GLONASS/BDS/Galileo positioning, NFC, and USB Type-C 2.0 ports, alongside stereo loudspeakers but no headphone jack. It is available in Infinite Black, Glacier Blue, or Viva Magenta colors with a price point starting around €875 globally (approximately $410/£769/₹80k depending on region).
